body: To exercise status-only vs bundled spec+status PATCH behavior for provisioning kinds, call helper.Repositories.Resource.Patch / helper.Connections.Resource.Patch with types.JSONPatchType and pass "status" as the subresource argument. Use the generic readConditions[T]/waitForConditionTypes[T] helpers (parameterized by a getConditions func like repositoryConditions/connectionConditions) instead of writing a per-kind condition reader - the old per-kind readRepositoryConditions/getRepositoryConditions/waitForConditionTypes were removed in favor of this. Assert via a unique condition type the controller never reconciles (not a controller-owned field like status.health), since the controller writes status concurrently and would race a direct value assertion.

search: Testing status-subresource PATCH semantics in provisioning integration tests uses the pattern: call helper.Repositories.Resource.Patch or helper.Connections.Resource.Patch with types.JSONPatchType and pass "status" as the subresource argument to exercise status-only vs bundled spec+status PATCH behavior. Use the generic readConditions[T] and waitForConditionTypes[T] helpers (parameterized by getConditions functions like repositoryConditions or connectionConditions) rather than writing per-kind condition readers; the old readRepositoryConditions/getRepositoryConditions were removed. Assert via a unique condition type the controller never reconciles—not controller-owned fields like status.health—to avoid races from concurrent controller writes. See pkg/tests/apis/provisioning/status_patch_test.go and repository_conditions_patch_test.go.
